children: Policymakers at Chile's central bank made a unanimous decision to leave the benchmark interest rate unchanged at 4.5% last week as uncertainty remained higher than usual, the minutes of this month's meeting showed on Wednesday.

• Holding the rate at the level at which it has been since December 2025 was consistent with the central bank's analysis and baseline scenario in the September Monetary Policy Report, the minutes showed.
• The minutes noted that Chile's inflation was evolving as forecast and was expected to converge to 3% in the second quarter of next year.
• Board members warned that the macroeconomic outlook remained subject to a higher degree of uncertainty than usual.
• Risks linked to the Middle East conflict persisted and had intensified recently, the minutes added.
• All board members said it was necessary to keep evaluating alternative scenarios that could require adjustments to monetary policy to ensure inflation converges to target.
